sha256-domain-v1.description: NodeID digest = SHA-256(domain_separation || 0x00 || profile_id UTF-8 || 0x00 || identity public key bytes). The identity public key is the STABLE identity-role public material; rotating operational keys never participate in derivation. Domain separation binds the digest to this derivation rule and profile.

description: Registry of ADCOS identity profiles (WORK-004). A profile is explicit metadata: NodeID derivation rule, key roles, and supported signing algorithms — never a hidden implementation convention. Cryptographic providers are replaceable and declare the algorithms they implement; the identity core never branches on a specific algorithm. NodeID is derived ONLY from the stable identity-role public key (and the profile), so operational-key rotation and revocation never change it (LOCK-005, LOCK-015).

identity.sha256-ecdsa-p256.v1.description: ECDSA P-256 (SECP256R1) profile. Requires a provider implementing alg.ecdsa-p256 (e.g. a hardware-backed or library provider in the reference implementation); the identity core only consumes the declared identifiers.

identity.sha256-ed25519.v1.description: Ed25519 profile. Requires a provider implementing alg.ed25519; the identity core only consumes the declared identifiers.

identity.sha256-hmac-dev.v1.description: DEVELOPMENT/TEST-ONLY profile using HMAC-SHA256 (a standard symmetric primitive) so the complete identity lifecycle can be exercised deterministically and offline with zero third-party dependencies. Because HMAC is symmetric, the public material stored for its credentials is a SHA-256 key fingerprint, and verification requires store-held key material; it MUST NOT be used where external public verification is required. Real deployments use the asymmetric profiles above with appropriate providers.

unknown_id_policy: A well-formed identifier matching the id_grammar but not present in this registry is UNKNOWN, not invalid. Unknown profile identifiers must be preserved verbatim in metadata and error reporting, must never be coerced to a registered profile, and must fail closed when used for identity operations. A malformed identifier (not matching the id_grammar) is INVALID and is rejected by parsers.
